successors.name: Qin (state)
successors.text: the Yiqu land as the page places it: 'the Hetao region, present-day Ningxia, eastern Gansu, and northern Shaanxi'

ledger.x: c. 720 BC: the Yiqu Rong are first on record. Infobox 'Founded: c. 720 BC, no earlier than the death of King Ping that year'; 'the Yiqu Rong migrated east', 'the first mention of Yiqu in textual sources'. (The page itself dates the Zhou move east to 770; the 720 is the page's.) The region is the researcher's reading…
318 BC: Yiqu beats Qin at Libo.
315 BC: the fighting of 318 ends with the cession of twenty-five cities to Qin (de facto end).
272 BC: Qin takes what is left of Yiqu.

wars.name: Qin submission of Yiqu
wars.outcome: Yiqu submitted to Qin as a vassal and Qin set up a county in its territory.

wars.name: Battle of Libo and the cession of 315
wars.outcome: Yiqu beat Qin at Libo in 318 but suffered a heavy defeat soon after and ceded twenty-five cities in 315.

wars.name: Qin attack on Yiqu under King Wu
wars.outcome: 'King Wu of Qin attacked Yiqu in the second year of his reign' (c.

wars.name: Destruction of Yiqu by Qin
wars.outcome: The Queen Dowager Xuan had the Yiqu king killed in 272 BC; Qin destroyed Yiqu and formed the Longxi, Beidi and Shang commanderies in its lands and built long walls.

certainty.note: No Yiqu boundary is documented; only the Hetao/Ningxia/eastern Gansu/northern Shaanxi description and the cities.
